findings.claim: iteration-1-benchmark.md showed placeholder zeros that contradicted results.md
the scripted checks behind 4/4 were not kept

grade.py maps run folders to type folders by hard-coded eval names (tutorial-getting-started, howto-supersede, ...) that evals.json never records, so a fresh skill-creator run with other folder names stops with a KeyError

verdict.text: Both findings sent back are fixed.
The broken benchmark file is gone, and the grading is kept as grade.py plus expectations in evals.json.
I reran grade.py on a copy of the iteration-1 runs and got 4/4 for all eight runs, and it catches a broken run when I break one.
Rows r1 to r3 still hold.
One small hardening note on grade.py, which does not block.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests and eval-row r1 pass; "stamp green: f837ee6309a3f3124a78c3fa65de6448cf58acd6d5600483776a1bc2258c8dc0".
The fingerprint matches the round-2 placeholder binding.
f1: plugin/skills/write-docs/evals/ holds only evals.json, grade.py and results.md; no benchmark file remains, and nothing in plugin/ or tests/ mentions one.
f2: evals.json gives each prompt an `expectations` list; the four scripted ones match the expectation texts grade.py writes, and the judged ones are marked "(judged ...)".
results.md names evals.json and grade.py.
I copied iteration-1 into my scratch folder and ran `KMCTL_BIN=.../write-docs-eval/bin python -I grade.py <copy>`: 4/4 for all eight runs.
To check the grader can fail, I deleted the how-to line from one run's docs/README.md: that run dropped to 2/4 (not listed, kmctl check fails), so the checks are real.
r1: unchanged test; passes in the stamp.
r2: SKILL.md is unchanged by the fix; still holds.
r3: four prompts, one per type, are kept; results.md and the regraded runs show every page in its type folder.
Holds.
f1: resolved.
The file was deleted.
f2: resolved.
evals.json has the expectations; grade.py is kept and reruns to the recorded scores.
f3: grade.py's FOLDER table keys on run folder names like `howto-supersede`, which appear only in the eval_metadata.json of the scratch run, not in the kept evals.json.
Regrading the existing run works, but a new skill-creator run whose folders are named otherwise stops with a KeyError.
Non-blocking hardening: adding a `name` to each evals.json entry (or mapping by id) is a plain fix and changes no skill behavior.
